status.summary: Lost a five-round main event to Tom Nolan by TKO (elbows from half guard) at 1:28 of round 3 (UFC Fight Night: Moicano vs. Nolan, Las Vegas, Oct 31, 2026). He controlled 7:09 of the first two rounds, then Nolan dropped him in round 2 and finished him from the top. Before that he submitted Chris Duncan with a rear-naked choke in round 2 (Apr 4, 2026), and lost to Islam Makhachev for the lightweight title (D'Arce choke, R1, UFC 311, Jan 18, 2025) and to Beneil Dariush (UD, UFC 317, Jun 28, 2025). A planned Brian Ortega fight at UFC 326 fell through when Ortega withdrew in January 2026. No bout booked. Age 37.
status.ranking: Unconfirmed. An MMA Mania UFC rankings-update headline after Oct 31, 2026 says Tom Nolan boots Renato Moicano from the lightweight top 10 (headline only; the article could not be opened on Nov 6)

style.summary: A submission-first lightweight who punches behind a head-heavy mix, then looks for the takedown, the back and the rear-naked choke; all seven of his UFC submissions are RNCs. At 155 his output on the feet is low and more of his damage is done on the ground (40% of landed significant strikes over three years). His chin is the main risk: four KO/TKO losses, the latest to Tom Nolan in October 2026.

moves.notes: Target split from fighters.json: decayed significant attempts are 85% head, 9% body, 6% legs (landed 78/13/9); career attempts 82/8/10, with leg kicks heavier in his featherweight years (38 leg strikes landed vs Kattar). So head punches carry most of the weight, and body and leg weights are low and roughly equal. Jab and cross lead as a judgment: ufcstats records target and position, not technique, and no scouting breakdown could be opened this pass (web search budget exhausted). Spinning is zero (none in his UFC finishes or records). Knees and elbows are small: 4.5% of decayed landed strikes come in the clinch, and his ground damage is filed by ufcstats as ground strikes without technique.

engine_notes.note: Chin: 5 knockdowns absorbed and 4 KO/TKO losses in 21 UFC fights; 1.30 knockdowns per 100 significant head strikes absorbed, time-decayed (shrunk 1.09), against a lightweight league rate of 0.95.

Control without safety: 345 s of control per 15 min decayed (league 174), yet takedown defense is 47% decayed. Against Nolan he held 7:09 of control in R1-R2 and still lost: Nolan dropped him in R2 and landed 30 ground strikes in R3.
Output rises within three-round fights (landed per minute 1.00, 1.40, 1.45 of R1 over 15 bouts). The five-round curve is noise: only the 2022 dos Anjos loss reached round 5.
Every UFC submission win is a rear-naked choke, so the director should route his finishes through back takes.
